name: Tsung-Chi Lin
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
fitReason: Strong physically grounded HRI and robotics-software fit, with current NJIT work on autonomous manipulation corrected through speech or teleoperation. A CS student could contribute interaction algorithms, perception/control integration or rigorous evaluation. The inspected packing system uses constrained symbolic preference updates rather than foundation-model semantic reasoning or learned low-level motor control.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full September 2026 NJIT-affiliated preprint Pack It My Way deploys a Kinova Gen3 7-DoF arm with Robotiq gripper, global Orbbec camera, wrist camera, marker-based perception and autonomous Cartesian pick-and-place. Twelve local-university adults compare human-expert mediation against a voice agent. Whisper small.en transcribes speech, then an explicitly deterministic parser updates a relational placement goal reused after object rearrangement. The paper explicitly excludes a general-purpose LLM and does not train a new manipulation policy.

shortVisit.summary: The full lab Openings page invites PhD, MS and undergraduate inquiries with CV, research statement and code/paper links, but does not explicitly identify external short-term visitors or summer duration. The team roster separately lists an external visiting student from National Taiwan Ocean University in spring 2026, providing precedent only. July 2026 visiting-university bootcamp sessions are educational events, not research internship openings.

unknowns: Eight-week hosting, visitor category, international sponsorship, funding and wholly personal support remain unknown.
The generic MS recruitment invitation does not establish an external master's short-visit route; the visiting-student roster is history, not availability.

The 2026 packing paper is a preprint; no conference acceptance was inferred. Its constrained parser and relational goal updates must not be described as open-ended LLM reasoning or learned robot policy.
Earlier TIAGo teleoperation work involved Johns Hopkins collaborators; the primary current-local evidence used here is the NJIT packing study.
The lab launched in August 2025 according to its news page, and current lab supervision/hardware access still require host agreement.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
